agents.note: One Google ADK LlmAgent named scope_safety_router.

tools.note: Five banking tools and eight observability/safety tools are bound through ALL_TOOLS.

authority.fact: The agent can read account balances, transactions, accounts and audit/escalation data, subject to in-tool IAM checks.
transfer_money mutates balances and writes transaction records but enforces ownership and sufficient-balance checks.
resolve_escalation_ticket mutates escalation state and performs a deterministic permission check.
Agent-level before/after model callbacks are commented out; safety is exposed as model-invoked tools and enforced primarily by prompt instructions.

policy_expectations.reason: The privileged ADK agent binds banking/state-changing tools while source-level tool-control callback/plugin/confirmation is not active; the callbacks are commented out.
transfer_money is a state-changing tool with no explicit human approval boundary, despite deterministic ownership checks and prompt-driven safety workflow.
The same agent combines sensitive banking data read authority with state-changing transfer/escalation authority.

Privileged banking writes are exposed to the model; deterministic IAM constrains resource scope but does not constitute human approval. Whether HorusTrace treats the model-mediated safety tools as a sufficient guardrail requires policy-semantic comparison.
